text: [{"id":10,"latex":"iii) The Problem of Arbitrariness: We argued that value subjectivism makes the attitudes or commands of the relevant person or group arbitrary. Such questions as 'Why should we obey arbitrary rules?' and 'How would someone's approving of $x$ for no reason make $x$ good?' then seem appropriate. Humor subjectivism, likewise, makes our laughter arbitrary—not in the sense that it cannot be causally explained, but in the sense that it cannot be justified. But this is not disturbing at all, in the way that arbitrariness in ethics would be. The question 'Why should we laugh at that joke?' does not naturally arise, and 'How would our being disposed to laugh at $x$ for no reason make $x$ funny?' seems uncompelling—we do not generally expect people to have reasons (that is, justifications) for laughter, in the sense that we might have reasons for our actions."}]
